title: the sudo relay's record proof generates its 10000-character output inside the shell, not in argv
intention: test_record_is_permanent_and_complete submits a short command that generates the 10000 characters inside the shell, and still asserts the stored stdout is the full 10000, so the tooth runs on Windows.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: Git bash (C:/Program Files/Git/usr/bin/bash.exe) given bash -c with a command of 8000 characters ran; 9000 failed: the command line limit is about 8191 characters on Windows
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof that fails for the size of its own fixture's argv measures the fixture, not the record; Law 7: the record still stores the whole output, unchanged.
how: In cairn/devices/sudo_relay/proofs/test_sudo_relay.py change the command to `head -c 10000 /dev/zero | tr '\0' x` and keep big = 'x' * 10000 for the length assertion. Declare the tooth under the new ticket in PROVES. No change to relay.py: the ~8191-character command limit of Git bash on Windows is recorded in measured as a standing limit of local_executor there.

clauses.claim: test_record_is_permanent_and_complete passes on Windows, where it failed once local_executor ran Git bash
the tooth still asserts len(record['stdout']) == 10000, so a truncating record still reds it

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: STANDING LIMIT, not fixed here: any production relay command over about 8191 characters now fails on Windows through local_executor (it passes the command as argv to bash -c); on Linux the limit is far higher
measured.how: same measurement; the relay's production callers were not censused for command length: HYPOTHESIS that none comes near it
